A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLIP and ObjaScale, despite the changed title and substantial method revision. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation and runtime results in Table 1, plus object-size and token-budget experiments in Figures 7, 9, and 10.

after.justification: V2 reports original results across six datasets, including architectural ablations, hierarchical inference comparisons, and small-object evaluations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: V2 replaces v1's separate perceptual/positional codes and patch decoder with pixel-query attention and sparse mask prediction. Positional embeddings now enter values as well as queries and keys, and normalization changes. The mask/position/box objective becomes adaptive sparse BCE training. Controlled patch overlap, 5-sigma inference bounds, and optional hierarchical refinement also change the procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds COCO and LVIS evaluation, substantially extending natural-image instance-segmentation coverage, including large-vocabulary annotations. Hypersim, KITTI-360, OpenImages, and ObjaScale remain. Both versions train on the Segment Anything dataset, called SA-1B in v2; that naming change does not add training coverage.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates SAM-B/L/H and FastSAM-s/x. V2 retains these and adds MobileSAM and EfficientSAM-T/S to the main comparison, introducing two relevant efficient segmentation families. Figure 7 also adds EfficientSAM-S and MobileSAM to the retained ObjaScale heatmap comparison.

E3.justification: The reported training schedule changes from approximately 1.5M updates with successive 128/512/4096-token phases to 2.7–8.5M updates, depending on model size, with tokens varied around 512. Three model configurations become four spanning 0.51–96.6M parameters. V2 also introduces architectural controls, standard versus hierarchical inference comparisons, a below-1%-area evaluation subset, and six-dataset averages.

E4.justification: V2 adds six architectural ablations addressing positional embeddings, normalization, patch-size limits, and adaptive sampling, evaluated with both inference modes in Table 2. Table 3 adds systematic small-object analysis across datasets. Scale heatmaps remain and expand, but v1's token-budget sensitivity experiment in Figure 9 is removed.

E5.justification: V1's Figure 10 reports 95% confidence bands, and Figure 9 includes a band labeled '50% quantile'; both plots disappear. Mean ± standard deviation IoU reporting remains in v2's tables. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or seeds, and the additional table rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 substantially replaces and expands the results. For example, Table 1 reports ObjaScale IoU of 89.02% for FLIP-Large (96.6M parameters), versus 84.94% for v1's FLIP-L (26.5M); changed architecture and training prevent treating this as a controlled gain. FastSAM-x's Hypersim IoU also changes from 43.39% to 34.36%. New baseline, dataset, ablation, hierarchical-inference, and small-object results are added.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes substantially: v1's perceptual/positional code definitions, Gaussian output-patch construction, and three-loss formulation are removed. V2 defines revised attention computations, pixel-query prediction, sparse BCE, 5-sigma inference bounds, and logarithmic refinement depth, alongside new computational-complexity arguments. These are substantive mathematical changes, although neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 claims performance approaching SAM while surpassing FastSAM and emphasizes interpretable separation of identity and location. V2 drops that disentanglement contribution and claims superior aggregate accuracy over SAM variants, over 1000-fold parameter savings for FLIP-Tiny, and approximately sixfold faster FLIP-Large inference. Energy savings and real-time applicability receive stronger emphasis in the abstract and contributions.

C2.justification: V2 removes the strict what/where separation explanation and adds substantive interpretations of sparse boundary sampling, architectural robustness, patch-size tradeoffs, and hierarchical inference's accuracy/runtime compromise. Sections 4.3–4.6 discuss these mechanisms and applicability implications. The absolute-pixel-size explanation remains, while v1's caveat about unoptimized patch-processing time disappears.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation documentation, including bilinear patch extraction, spatial hashing and a Python C extension, MLP and residual-scaling details, seven sampling-distance bins, 2048 sampled pixels, and refinement defaults. It adds RTX4090 timing hardware and a project-page link. The newly stated 256-pixel ObjaScale object-size cap documents generation more precisely without establishing that the dataset changed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds discussion and citations for EfficientSAM, MobileSAM, and TinyViT, and the evaluation adds COCO/LVIS references. The Xiong et al. (2020) normalization reference is removed. The Related Work section and the central positioning against full-image encoding largely remain, making this a limited literature expansion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The method narrative replaces the what/where subsection with pixel prediction and explicit inference descriptions, while the results section is reorganized around overall performance, efficiency, small objects, ablations, and generalization. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: Architecture diagrams are redrawn, a Pixel-Predictor diagram and runtime plot are added, and Figure 7 expands from three to five heatmaps. Figure 1 changes from ObjaScale-only to six-dataset averages. Table 1 expands while losing its timing breakdown, and Tables 2–3 are added. V1's sampling diagram and two curve plots disappear; the KITTI and ObjaScale example displays are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked component ablations and comparisons with lightweight transformer baselines. V2's Tables 1–3 address these important validation gaps and examine the accuracy/runtime tradeoff, while expanded implementation and hardware details improve assessability. These gains substantially strengthen support for the central efficiency claim. They outweigh the removed token-budget/uncertainty plots and timing breakdown, although energy-saving claims lack direct measurements and Figure 8 ambiguously labels hierarchical results without their suffixes.
